prompt: State two assumptions of the ideal gas model.
markscheme: Any two **(A2)**: particles have negligible volume; there are no intermolecular forces; collisions are perfectly elastic; particles move randomly in straight lines between collisions.

prompt: Explain why real gases deviate most from ideal behaviour at low temperature and high pressure.
markscheme:
At high pressure particles are close together, so their own volume is a significant fraction of the container volume **(R1)**

At low temperature particles move slowly, so intermolecular attractions become significant **(R1)**; attractions reduce the pressure exerted, so $PV<nRT$ **(R1)**

prompt: What volume does 4.40 g of carbon dioxide occupy at STP (273 K, 100 kPa; molar volume $22.7\ \text{dm}^{3}\,\text{mol}^{-1}$)? ($M=44.0$)
markscheme: **B.** $n=0.100$ mol; $V=0.100\times22.7=2.27\ \text{dm}^{3}$. The molar volume is the same for every ideal gas at a given T and P.

prompt: 0.500 g of a gas occupies 250 cm³ at 25 °C and 101 kPa. Calculate its molar mass. ($R=8.31\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$)
markscheme:
Convert units: $V=2.50\times10^{-4}\ \text{m}^{3}$, $T=298$ K, $P=1.01\times10^{5}$ Pa **(A1)**

$n=\dfrac{PV}{RT}=0.0102$ mol **(M1)(A1)**

$M=\dfrac{0.500}{0.0102}=49.1\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$ **(A1)**

**Common mistake:** using cm³ and kPa directly — with $R=8.31$ the units must be Pa and m³.
